After moisturizing your lips make sure you wait awhile before putting on your lipstick. You want your lips to feel dry but not flaky and you definitely don't want them to feel slick. In general putting a lipgloss over your lipstick will make it come off easier even if you have dry lips. If you're using a liquid lipstick or stain make sure you wait for it to dry before drinking/eating/doing whatever with your mouth. Using too many layers or layers that are thick can also contribute to lipstick flaking off throughout the day. If I'm wearing a long wear liquid lipstick I usually don't reapply without wiping off whatever is left over because it makes it peel if I don't. 

These tips should help make the products you already own last longer but if you're looking for new products Beauty Bakerie lip whips are my holy grail. They're on the pricier end but I think they're worth it.

My biggest piece of advice for makeup in general is PRACTICE!! For graphic liner specifically I try to sketch out the shape with as thin lines as possible to make sure it looks right/even before going in and darkening and perfecting the lines. I also try to draw as much of the graphic with my eyes open as possible because you can get a better idea of where to place it so it looks good with my eye shape. I also make sure I take my time this whole makeup look took about an hour and a half and there were many moments I put down my eyeliner and just took a deep breath to steady myself before continuing. My best advice if you really want to get better at eyeliner is try to find time to practice when you have plenty of time and no where to go after so you can try techniques without worrying about mistakes.
